A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same ZeroFlow work. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including visual verification of the new hybrid results. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning accuracy, forgetting, memory, and runtime measurements, together with query-budget and optimization analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds accuracy curves comparing hybrid first-order/zeroth-order training with first-order training.

M1.justification: Section 6 adds Hybrid ZO, which first optimizes with first-order gradients and then switches to zeroth-order refinement. This is an additional procedure; the existing ZO formulation, historical-gradient mixing, and random sparsification remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The four named datasets—CIFAR-100, CUB, ImageNet-A, and OmniBenchmark—and class-incremental task remain. However, the new hybrid experiment in Figure 7 does not identify its dataset, preventing reliable determination of whether it extends coverage or uses retained data.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain FO-SGD, FO-Adam, the ZO, Sign, and Conserve variants, and Forward-Grad. The new hybrid study uses an FO comparator. EASE was already evaluated in v1; its added citation does not introduce a baseline.

E3.justification: The hybrid experiment introduces switching from FO training to ZO refinement within the plotted 200-epoch runs. Its timing is inconsistently reported: Section 6 specifies 140 or 160 initial FO epochs, whereas Figure 7 labels 140 and 170. The existing benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 examines when ZO refinement helps, comparing two switching times with FO training across five task panels. The existing query-budget sweep, trajectory analyses, historical-gradient proportions, and sparsity sweep are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new hybrid curves likewise provide no statistical uncertainty reporting; the existing seed-based sparsification mask is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds hybrid accuracy curves showing larger advantages over FO in Tasks 3–5. Table 2 removes six OmniBenchmark runtime entries, including FO-SGD's 109.6 seconds and ZO-SGD's 66.8 seconds at q=1. Tables 1, 3, and 4, and the retained Table 2 values, are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The SPSA expression, replay and regularization losses, and historical-gradient mixing formula are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is reformatted without mathematical revision. The hybrid addition includes no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the claimed contribution from two enhancement techniques to three, incorporating Hybrid ZO. The central benchmark and forward-pass claims remain. The conclusion still refers to two enhancements, leaving an inconsistency.

C2.justification: v3 explains hybrid gains through flatter-region refinement and recovery of generalization after early incremental stages. It removes v1's specific warning that excessive sparsity can eliminate important gradient components, impair new-task learning, and worsen forgetting.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page address and a statement promising code upon publication; neither establishes an actual code release. It also provides epoch counts for the new hybrid procedure, although these conflict with Figure 7.

R1.justification: v3 adds the EASE paper, Expandable Subspace Ensemble, and removes references to Delange et al.'s survey, Diao et al.'s black-box prompt learning, BBTv2, and Werbos's backpropagation-through-time work. The substantive positioning around gradient-free optimization otherwise remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and the seven-section sequence remain. Local revisions condense Section 6, label its three enhancements, replace Section 2's numbered subsections with paragraph headings, update author/contact information, switch citation style, and add a generic Impact Statement.

P2.justification: v3 adds the five-panel Figure 7 and relocates the former Figure 7 as Figure 8. Table 2 becomes a single-column table, Table 1 gains bold score emphasis, and the document receives revised title formatting, running headers, page numbers, and float placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a potentially useful hybrid study and improves attribution and access information. However, that experiment leaves its dataset/model unspecified and reports conflicting switch epochs, limiting the added evidence's interpretability. It also removes OmniBenchmark runtimes and the excessive-sparsity caution while retaining the core benchmark results. These benefits and losses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
